## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).

# Handoff: remove the brain-local privacy layer (tombstones, gates, privacy commands)

## Decision context (already made — do not re-litigate)

The brain is a derived index over git-resident checkpoints (`entire/checkpoints/v1`
branch and `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`, read via `git cat-file`). Deletion
originates in the capture layer: `entire checkpoint delete` removes a checkpoint
from the v1 branch tip, locally and on checkpoint remotes. The brain's job is to
mirror git: when a checkpoint is gone from the refs, the brain drops everything
derived from it at the next refresh.

The brain-local privacy layer (session tombstones + exclude/include/purge +
read gates) was an explicit stopgap "until a capture-layer exclusion contract
exists" (commit `4b5cdfd3`, 2026-08-07). That contract direction is now chosen.
PR #586 already retired the instant-suppression guarantee: retrieval emission no
longer takes any lock; a policy change takes effect on the next command. This
task removes the rest of the layer.

Approved rules:
- Facts: on rebuild, drop provenance entries citing sessions whose checkpoints
  are gone; drop a distilled fact only when it has no provenance left. Authored
  facts (`remember`, no session anchor) are never touched.
- Hosted retraction of already-synced facts is OUT OF SCOPE: the nightly job
  handles it.
- Deletion converges at the next refresh (the watch daemon ticks anyway).
  "Stop serving now" = `entire checkpoint delete … && entire brain refresh`.
  Document this; do not rebuild any per-response enforcement.

## What to delete

1. Tombstone store and flows: `internal/cli/internal/brainstore/tombstones.go`,
   `read_guard.go` consumers, `session_privacy.go` / `session_privacy_verify.go`
   (exclude/include/purge executors, privacy transactions, rollback machinery),
   the `privacy` command family (list/exclude/include/purge).
2. Read gates: `requirePrivacyDerivedRead`, `privacyDerivedReadGate`,
   `internal/cli/patterns/derived_gate.go` (DerivedReadGate / RequireDerivedRead),
   `revalidateRetrievalResponsePrivacy`, and the per-response policy machinery:
   `CaptureRetrievalPrivacyPolicy`, `ValidateRetrievalPrivacyPolicies`,
   `WithLockedRetrievalPrivacyPolicies`, `RetrievalPrivacyPolicy`,
   `commitRetrievalResponse`'s validation, the race seams
   (`beforeRetrievalResponsePrivacyRecheck`,
   `beforeRetrievalResponsePrivacyEmissionCheck`).
3. The locked mutation wrappers that exist only for policy linearization:
   `runPrivacyLinearizedPatternMutation` (5 call sites: recall_evidence is
   already off it; patterns verify self-locks via
   `patterncore.WithCorpusMutationLocked`; check each remaining site for what
   mutual exclusion its body actually needs and give it a direct lock), and the
   member-policy locks in `BuildWorkspaceCorpus`
   (`internal/cli/patterns/workspace_corpus.go:91`). Note the comment at
   `workspace_patterns.go:745`: workspace verify and skill synthesis use those
   locks as mutual exclusion against each other — replace with an explicit
   workspace-brain lock, not silence.
4. Tombstone-aware ingestion: `partitionTombstonedSessions` in export, the
   history/conversation index skip of excluded sessions, doctor's privacy
   states, viz guard plumbing (`Server.Guard`, `requestSessionGuard`,
   `privacyResponseMiddleware` policy capture — the middleware can likely go
   entirely; response buffering too, unless kept for write-error atomicity).
5. Output buffering (`bufferRetrievalCommandOutput`) exists only for the
   privacy boundary. Optional: keep the buffering (it also prevents partial
   output on render errors) but strip the policy parameter. Judgment call;
   do not keep dead parameters.

## What to add

1. Strict-mirror sweep: refresh drops every brain artifact not reachable from
   current checkpoint refs. Remove the deliberate retain-last-copy behavior in
   `internal/cli/export.go` (~lines 403-419: unavailable sessions' cached
   transcripts are kept as "the only surviving copy" — that contradicts the
   mirror model).
2. Provenance-based fact drop in refresh/rebuild, per the approved rule above.
   Facts carry `provenance[].session_id`; sessions present = sessions in the
   current checkpoint catalog.
3. A replacement for the privacy canary test: plant a secret in one session of
   a test repo's checkpoint branch, delete that checkpoint from the v1 tip,
   run refresh, assert the secret is absent from the sessions tree, history
   index, FTS, conversation store, and facts, while other sessions survive.
   The old canary (purge-based) goes with the purge command.

## Known coordination points

- `entire checkpoint delete` is per-checkpoint and leaves sibling checkpoints
  of the same session; a session-level delete and a merge-surviving deletion
  record (anti-resurrection across clones) belong to the entire CLI repo, not
  this task. The brain-side mirror is correct regardless: it reflects whatever
  the refs say.
- The tegucigalpa workspace is consolidating per-branch fact stores into one
  flat per-repo store (see plan-single-repo-fact-store.md there) — this
  REPLACED the branch-pruning task. It rewrites `updateFactSourceManifestLocked`,
  the factstore package, and parts of export.go. Do not touch those; the
  single-store PRs should land first. Note: the purge-compat constraint
  ("payloads live in files old clients can purge") is why fact payloads still
  sit in legacy branch files — your removal of purge and that constraint's
  removal are the same event; coordinate timing.

## Validation

- Replacement canary above is the core proof.
- Expect large test deletions: everything asserting PrivacyDirtyCode flows,
  late-tombstone rejection, privacy commands, derived gates. Deleting a test is
  correct when the guarantee is retired; replacing it is required when the
  guarantee moved (canary).
- `gofmt -l -s` and `go vet` clean (CI gate; no oxfmt binary in this repo).
- Run `go test` directly on touched packages; `mise run check` fails locally
  for a missing gotestsum. The cli suite runs near the 600 s timeout.

## Evidence and history

- Brain memories (branch `main` unless noted): `fact:1d10ce176f39425716a28b6e`
  (four-cause customer diagnosis, branch `evisdren/brain_locked-write.lock-fix`),
  `fact:6a5a0feef41ccfa33e37a291` (emission-lock fix decision),
  `fact:991cb0f38f554cd002f17967` (tombstone gate on read path — superseded by
  this work), `fact:4822420d42c08bb73645bdcd` (repo-wide write lock rationale).
- PR #586 (emission lock removal), commit `4b5cdfd3` (privacy layer
  introduction, states the stopgap intent in its message).
- Retrieve more with:
  `entire brain recall "<question>" --branch main --json`

+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
+- The brain-local privacy layer: the `privacy` command family
+  (`list|exclude|include|purge|verify|retention`), session tombstones, read
+  gates, and the per-response privacy policy machinery. The brain is a
+  derived index that mirrors the repository's checkpoint refs, so deletion
+  happens at the capture layer: `entire checkpoint delete` removes a
+  checkpoint, and the next `entire brain refresh` drops everything derived
+  from it — including the deleted session's fact provenance (a distilled
+  fact with no provenance left is deleted; authored memories and pulled
+  teammate copies are never touched). Caches of vanished sessions are swept
+  instead of retained. "Stop serving now" is
+  `entire checkpoint delete <checkpoint> && entire brain refresh`.
+
+++ b/README.md
+using an older client to clean up that store. An older client cannot remove
+that snapshot; a new-client migration repairs hidden snapshot residue and
+abandoned temporary files.
+++ b/docs/recall_threat_model.md
+- Deletion originates at the capture layer: `entire checkpoint delete`
+  removes a checkpoint from the v1 tip (locally and on checkpoint remotes),
+  and the brain mirrors the refs — the next `entire brain refresh` drops the
+  session's transcript, history records, conversation exchanges, pattern
+  episodes, caches and FTS entries, and the provenance anchors of its
+  distilled facts (a distilled fact with no provenance left is deleted;
+  authored memories are never touched). "Stop serving now" is
+  `entire checkpoint delete <checkpoint> && entire brain refresh`; the watch
+  daemon converges on its next tick. The mirror canary test plants a secret
+  in one checkpoint session, deletes it from the tip, refreshes, and asserts
+  the secret is absent from the sessions tree, history index, FTS,
+  conversation retrieval, and facts while other sessions survive.
+- **Convergence window**: deletion takes effect at the next refresh, not at
+  the next response. A response assembled between the checkpoint deletion and
+  the refresh can still carry the deleted session's content (the
+  instant-suppression guarantee was deliberately retired with the brain-local
+  privacy layer; enforcing it required a per-response lock that failed every
+  concurrent reader during long writes).
+- **Hosted copies**: facts already synced over the per-fact wire are not
+  retracted by a local refresh; the nightly hosted job handles retraction.
+- **Session-level delete and anti-resurrection**: `entire checkpoint delete`
+  is per-checkpoint and leaves sibling checkpoints of the same session; a
+  session-level delete and a merge-surviving deletion record across clones
+  belong to the capture layer (entire CLI).
+- **Vector stores** hold embeddings of session text; embedding inversion is a
+  known class of partial-content recovery. The mirror rebuild regenerates
+  them from surviving sessions.

content.text:
### Strengths

- The deletion is thorough. Tombstones, read gates, policy capture and validation, race seams, the viz middleware, the `privacy` commands, and `partitionTombstonedSessions` are all gone. `go build`, `go vet ./internal/cli/...`, and `gofmt -l -s` are clean.
- The lock replacements are correct. The old `runPrivacyLinearizedPatternMutation` and `CaptureWorkspaceDerivedReadPolicies` already held the repo or workspace brain write lock, so the new `WithBrainWriteLock` calls keep the same exclusion.
  - I traced `ProposeFamilies`, `synthesizeAndForm`/`recordSkillDecision`, `BuildWorkspaceCorpusLocked` and `VerifyDossiers`. None of them takes the same lock again, so there is no deadlock.
  - `RecoverWorkspaceCorpusPublication` and `BuildWorkspaceCorpus` lock for themselves, and every caller calls them outside a held lock.
- The `export.go` rewrite is equivalent to the old code when no session is exempt. `partitionLocalTranscriptSessions` keeps input order, so `sessions = usable` and the rebuilt `branchDirs` match the old surviving-session bookkeeping.
- The `history.go` identity rework is sound. With no tombstones, dropping the `Tombstones` component cannot weaken the prepare/commit staleness check.
- `facts_mirror.go` uses the same lock → write → `MigrateRepository` → `updateFactSourceManifestLocked` sequence as `reclassifyAllFactBranches`.
- The retrieval-filter removals (`retrieve.go`, `internal/retrieval/retrieve.go`, viz handlers, dash `SessionViews`) keep the duplicate-winner filtering, structured filters, limits and self-echo filtering.
- Tests: the canary, `TestVanishedSessionCacheIsSwept`, and the patterns, internal and command subpackage suites pass.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

1. **The fact mirror deletes facts for sessions that are still in the checkpoint catalog.** The spec says "sessions present = sessions in the current checkpoint catalog". `dropFactsForMissingSessions` (`internal/cli/facts_mirror.go`) reads `manifest.Sources.Sessions` instead. That list has already lost every session whose transcript bytes are unavailable locally (`export.go`, `sessions = usable`).
   - **Main trigger:** squash-merged manual-commit checkpoints. The old export comment counted 0 of 39 such IDs still resolving on a real repo.
   - **Proof:** I ran a probe in a temp copy using `vanishedCacheFixture`. I removed one transcript object and left the catalog entry, then ran an export and `dropFactsForMissingSessions`. Result: `deleted=1`, `facts left=0`.
   - **Where it runs:** on every refresh, including the unattended watch-daemon tick, and silently. On the first refresh after upgrade, a repo with many such sessions loses all facts distilled from them. Those facts cost tokens and cannot be rebuilt.
   - **Second trigger:** the hidden `refresh --checkpoint-limit N` and `--scope branch` flags write a partial manifest, so facts outside that window are deleted too.
   - **Fix:** take membership from the catalog (`selected`, before the availability partition). One way is to persist the catalog session IDs, or the IDs that were skipped as unavailable. Also skip the drop when the export was limited or branch-scoped.

#### Important (Should Fix)

1. **Mixed-provenance facts lose foreign anchors on every refresh.** `hasLocalProvenance` gates the whole fact, but `anchorPresent` then judges every anchor. A pulled-teammate anchor or a `mem0:` import anchor (session ID only, no transcript) is "missing" from the catalog by design, so it is removed even when nothing was deleted.
   - Probe: anchors `[local present, mem0:abc, teammate-session]` → `stripped=2`.
   - `UnionAnchors` in dedup and merge creates such facts. The `keepHostedFact` comment documents the case.
   - Effect: the fact is later deleted when its local session goes, even though a teammate or import source still supports it.
   - Fix: treat anchors that have no `Transcript` as unattributable and keep them, the same way the fact-level rule does.
2. **Session abstracts of a deleted session are never removed.** `history/abstracts/v1/*.json` holds LLM summaries of the transcript (overview, decisions). Abstract egress receipts are also kept.
   - The old purge removed them. Now `purgeSessionAbstractsForRefs`, `sessionRefsForSessionID` and `purgeAbstractEgressReceiptsForSessionRefs` are unreachable.
   - The abstracts stay on disk and are included in `bundle export --include-sessions` (the history layer skips only `tombstones.json`, `privacy` and `work`).
   - The docs say refresh "drops everything derived from it". The canary does not check abstracts.
3. **About 20 tests of guarantees unrelated to privacy were deleted with the privacy-named files.** In a temp copy I restored them unchanged (only a duplicate helper and one unused import removed), and all 17 I ran pass against HEAD.
   - The 17 I ran:
     - all 9 tests in `retrieval_guard_test.go`: fact-review IDs and aliases, pending-review annotations, malformed proposal-queue caveats, `CurrentCodeUnavailable` caveats.
     - 8 pattern-corpus publication tests from `pattern_privacy_publish_test.go`: crash boundaries, failed staging keeps the live corpus, directory-swap symlink safety, bounded and symlink-rejecting transcript reads, partial-publication refusal, newer-manifest refusal.
   - Also deleted and not privacy-specific (I read these but did not run them): `TestGetBatchCapsRequestSize`, `TestMemoryMigrationProgressRejectsFIFOBeforeOpen`, `TestAbstractLaneCancellationPollCancelsProviderAndSettlesJob`.
   - Fix: restore them in non-privacy files.
4. **Upgrade re-surfaces sessions that users excluded or purged.** A leftover `history/tombstones.json` is now ignored. Any excluded or purged session whose checkpoint still exists comes back into history, FTS, conversation, patterns and the sessions view at the next refresh.
   - Nothing warns the user, and the CHANGELOG does not tell users to run `entire checkpoint delete` for those sessions first.
   - A user who excluded a session that holds a secret would not expect this. At minimum, make refresh warn when the old tombstone file lists exclusions, and document the step.

### Declined to judge

- Corroborated facts keep text that the deleted session contributed. The spec rule keeps a fact while any provenance remains.
- Matching is per session, not per checkpoint, so a sibling checkpoint keeps the session alive. The spec puts session-level delete in the entire CLI.
- A user's own synced fact can come back on the next hosted pull after the mirror deletes it locally. Hosted retraction is out of scope, and the ledger ruling accepts the cost. The docs could say this.
- Viz pins the manifest at startup, so a deleted session's metadata shows until restart. Instant suppression was retired on purpose.
- Patterns verify, skills form and workspace verify hold the brain write lock across provider calls. The old policy lock did the same, so this is not a regression.
- The entity index keeps session-ID links (identifiers, not content) until the next backfill.
- Output buffering was removed from pattern mutations, and the viz middleware was removed (ledger rulings).
- The manifest keeps the `privacy_identity` and `excluded_sessions` fields (ledger ruling).
- `privacy retention` was deleted (ledger ruling).

### Verdict

Not ready to merge. Fix Critical 1 (catalog-based membership, and no drop for limited or branch-scoped exports) and Important 1–4 first. The lock work, the export rewrite and the history identity changes are sound.

I reviewed in three passes: production diff, new tests, then the test deletions. All probes ran in temp copies under `/tmp/review-mirror` and `/tmp/review-base`. The worktree was not changed.
